findings.description: Critical: The revised plan scopes the `escalate_resume` prior-record lookup by `lease_generation`, but it does not explicitly require the approval-reference authorization check used by resume to match that same generation. In the current code, `ExecutionAdapter.resume` validates only gate plus `dispatch_id` through `gate_router.require_approval_ref`, and `require_approval_ref` has no lease-generation parameter. That leaves a stale `gate-decision:<id>` capable of authorizing a later parked generation through the public resume path even though the router would correctly treat that later exhaustion as a new decision subject.
findings.resolution: Extend the plan/spec/tasks to require `lease_generation` in the recorded `escalate_resume` correlation and in the resume-time approval-ref check. `ExecutionAdapter.resume` or its private helper should pass the currently parked generation to `require_approval_ref`, and tests should prove an old proceed ref for generation N cannot resume generation N+1.

findings.description: Critical: D5 constrains route output fields and says policy-pause routing should use a fixed reason, but it still does not define an exact allowlist for the approval request/notification context that `ApprovalGate` forwards verbatim to `/approvals/request` and interpolates into the notification body. The phrase `such as` also leaves the fixed reason non-literal. Because this change makes the outbound approval path automatic at the failure boundary, implementers need an exact context contract, not just a prohibition on transcript/raw payload/child reason content.
findings.resolution: Add a concrete notification-context allowlist and bounds to the contract/spec, for example exactly `dispatch_id`, `change_id`, `item_id`, `verb`, and a literal fixed `reason` string for policy pauses. Add tests asserting the coordinator request context and notification body contain only those fields and never the child-provided parked reason, transcripts, raw approval payloads, or secret-like data.

findings.description: Nit: `tasks.md` requires Ruff, change plus repo-wide strict OpenSpec validation, deterministic context-drift checking, and scope checking, but `work-packages.yaml` only requires the supervise pytest suite, affected orchestration tests, and strict validation for this single change. A coordinated implementer can therefore satisfy the work-package evidence contract while skipping several validation tasks the plan says are required, including the scope check that guards runtime mirror synchronization.
findings.resolution: Add work-package verification steps for Ruff, repo-wide `openspec validate --strict --all`, the deterministic context-drift gate, and the post-sync scope check, or explicitly mark which task-list validations are manual handoff requirements outside the work-package evidence contract.

findings.description: Verified: The revised plan closes the round-1 apply-return-shape conflict. `ExecutionAdapter.apply` is specified to keep its existing return keys, while `route_parked_escalations` owns the separate bounded resolution list and is retryable after durable application.

Verified: The nested-lock deadlock disposition is substantively closed at the plan level. D2 requires exactly one workspace serialization boundary for routing and a private already-locked resume helper so `resolve_parked` can resume without calling the public lock-taking method.

Verified: The mirror/handoff gap is closed in the revised executable plan. Blocked routing relies on synchronous mirror projection, rehydrate prefers a newer mirror over stale or missing handoff state, and the next normal handoff carries the same pending gate and deadline.
